lyrics:
[Intro: lilting electric guitar figure in harmony, bass, light drums]

[Verse 1: warm, raspy, quick]
Down by the reservoir, shoes in the grass
A bottle of pop and a bus pass
Skipping every stone we found
Sun going down, sun going down

[Chorus: band lifts, tambourine]
Hey, Freckles, you and me
Halfway up the cherry tree
Hey, Freckles
I can still hear the two of us go
La-la, la-la-dee-dah
La-la, la-la-dee-dah

[Verse 2: warm, a little faster]
Behind the bandstand, sharing a coat
You wrote your name on my hand, and I wrote
Mine on yours, and it wouldn't come clean
We were ten, or we might have been thirteen

[Chorus: band lifts, tambourine]
Hey, Freckles, you and me
Halfway up the cherry tree
Hey, Freckles
I can still hear the two of us go
La-la, la-la-dee-dah
La-la, la-la-dee-dah

[Bass Break: bass plays the melody alone, then guitar answers]

[Verse 3: slower start, then picking up]
Now I'm sixty-eight and the tree's a stump
The reservoir's a car park with a speed bump
But a kid went by with a nose like yours
All dots, and I was back outdoors

[Final Chorus: full band, backing voices on the syllables]
Hey, Freckles, you and me
Halfway up the cherry tree
Hey, Freckles
I can still hear the two of us go
La-la, la-la-dee-dah
La-la, la-la-dee-dah

[Outro: guitar figure, syllables, fade]
La-la, la-la-dee-dah
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 150 BPM, 4/4, G major. A light, skipping beat with a Caribbean lilt. Sunny, loose and nostalgic.

VOICE: Male tenor, warm and raspy with a soul singer's phrasing and an Irish colour, sliding around the beat as if making it up. Backing voices join on the sung syllables in the last chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: Two electric guitars playing a bright, lilting figure in harmony a third apart. A melodic electric bass that takes a short solo. A light drum kit with a skipping pattern. Acoustic rhythm guitar. Tambourine. Soft backing voices.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the guitar figure. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:28 Chorus 1. 0:50 Verse 2. 1:08 Chorus 2. 1:30 Bass break. 1:44 Verse 3, starting slower and picking up. 2:06 Final chorus with backing voices. 2:30 Outro, the guitar figure and syllables fading by 2:50.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1960s pop-soul single: bright, warm and slightly rough, recorded quickly with a live feel.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The guitar figure in the first three seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original looks back a few years. This looks back nearly sixty, at places that are now a car park, and is set off by a stranger's child. It keeps the tune of happiness and adds the distance.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Memory, joy, a jolt of the present, joy again.
